title: Cala data-quality notes from Team Moonshot (Junction 2026)
context: Recount counts, per fund, how often it led a round. We asked Cala /v1/knowledge/query two ways: company-first (round history of each company) and investor-first (every round fund X invested in and whether X led it). Below is what we had to clean up to count leads reliably, offered as a thank-you. Some drift comes from our own free-form prompts; we flag it because a fixed schema would help every user.

histories.jsonl.query: List every funding round of {company} with announcement date, round type, amount, lead investor and all participating investors

funds.jsonl.query: List every funding round that {X} invested in ... and whether {X} led the round (some funds queried per year)
funds.jsonl.note: file was still growing during analysis; counts reflect this snapshot

method: Python over the raw JSON answers; dates parsed to year-month, stages mapped from labels (pre-seed, seed, series a-f, growth), cross-path matches = same company name and dates within 2 months. No LLM was used to judge.
positives: Answers include entities[] with stable-looking IDs and the mention text, which made most of this checkable.
Ambiguous queries are refused with an explanation (company 'Elmo') rather than answered with a guess.

findings.description: The same question template returns the same concept under different field names from answer to answer. Across 3016 rows we saw 91 distinct field sets. Our prompts did not fix a schema, so some drift is expected, but a fixed output schema (or a documented canonical name per concept) would remove a whole class of silent data loss: a parser that misses one alias silently drops the date or the co-investors for that row.

examples.note: Date under 'announcement' (10 rows use this key), next to 'announcement_date', 'date' and 'announced' elsewhere.
Investor-first answers use 'company' or 'company_name', 'country' or 'company_country', 'date' or 'announcement_date'.

findings.description: The 'did fund X lead?' flag comes back as a JSON boolean in some answers and as free text in others: 642 of 1167 flag values are strings ('Yes', 'No', 'Yes (co-lead)', 'Co-led', 'Not confirmed', 'Unknown', 'Likely co-led', 'Details limited'). The key name also varies for one fund ('lifeline_led' and 'lifeline_ventures_led' for Lifeline Ventures) and is abbreviated for another ('cv_led' for Contrarian Ventures). A tri-state boolean plus a separate co_lead flag would make this field directly countable.

examples.note: String 'Yes (co-led)' where other answers use true.
Two key names for the same flag across yearly queries of the same fund

findings.description: The investor-first answer's '<fund>_led' flag sometimes contradicts the lead_investor field: in the company-first answer for the same round (5 contradictions among rounds we could match across both paths), or in the same row (10 rows have the flag true while lead_investor is null). One row also names the lead with a typo ('Voita Ventures' for Voima Ventures, Iiwari seed). For anyone counting who leads, this is the most important field.

findings.description: We matched 98 rounds that appear in both an investor-first and a company-first answer (same company, dates within 2 months). In 23 of them the labels disagree: 13 map to two different stages (for example Series C vs Series D, Seed vs Series A) and 10 give a stage in one answer and a generic label ('Other', 'Funding Round', 'Undisclosed', 'Equity + Debt') in the other. Stage is what founders filter on, so a single canonical label per round (with the raw label kept alongside) would help.

Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Mikko Kodisoja Foundation, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

findings.description: The same investor appears under several spellings in the free-text investor fields, sometimes with acronyms, legal suffixes or renames in brackets. For five investors we checked by pattern there are 43 distinct strings. The entities[] list helps (it resolves mentions to IDs), but the round fields themselves carry only text, so counting needs fuzzy matching. Returning entity IDs inline in lead_investor and participating_investors would solve this.

49 exact names (case-insensitive) of companies, organisations or people resolve to more than one entity ID across answers. Some may be genuinely different legal entities sharing a name; we have not verified each one. For investors such as Global Founders Capital or Target Global this splits one fund into several graph nodes.

17 exact names carry different entity_type values in different answers (mostly Company vs Organization; EIT InnoEnergy is Organization in one answer and EducationalInstitution in another). Investor typing (fund, angel, corporate, public body) is not available.

The same company asked under two names (both names are in common use) returns two different round histories. In investor-first answers, aliases are carried inside the company string ('Verda (DataCrunch)', 'Verda (fka DataCrunch)', 'Riff (fka Databutton)', 'Riff (formerly Databutton)'), 49 distinct company strings carry an alias, a bracketed note or a slash. A company entity ID per row would let consumers merge these safely.

findings.description: 26 pairs of rows in company-first answers share a stage and fall within 3 months of each other. Many are real tranches or extensions, which is correct to report, but there is no parent-round key, and some totals include the earlier tranche, so summing rows double counts. One answer split a single round into one row per co-investor. A round_group_id plus a flag for "amount is cumulative" would fix both.

rows.amount: $200 million (total, inclusive of the $75 million Dexcom tranche)

examples.note: Second row amount includes the first: summing gives USD 275M instead of 200M.
Debt row refers to the other row in text ('included in the $70 M above').
One Series A extension returned as three rows, one per participating investor.

findings.description: Investor fields often hold placeholder text instead of null: 120 lead fields and 386 participant fields contain phrases such as 'Not publicly disclosed', 'Undisclosed', 'and others', '+ 10 others' or 'Not Practica'. A naive parser turns these into investors called 'Undisclosed' or 'others'. Suggest null plus separate fields such as lead_disclosed=false and additional_investor_count.

Investor fields mix funds, angels and explanatory prose in one string. 114 rows carry a person role or note inside an investor name (e.g. '(Bolt co-founder)', '(led by Founding Partner ...)', or a sentence after a dash), and 146 rows carry a status in brackets ('(co-lead)', '(existing investor)', '(returning)'). Angels are often correct investors, but without a type the consumer cannot tell a fund from a person (391 Person entity IDs appeared in answers). Structured fields (investor_type, is_follow_on, note) would keep the names clean.

findings.description: 7 date values are truncated so the year is lost (for example "11 June 5" and "July 17, 5..."); 2 of them also contain a zero-width space inside the year ("23 July 5<U+200B>025"). Separately, 237 dates are ranges, alternatives or annotated ("May 3, 2018 (CB Insights) / October 1, 2018 (Tracxn)", "~Apr–May 2020"), and formats mix ISO, "Month D, YYYY", "D Month YYYY" and "Mon YYYY". In 11 investor-first rows the date field holds a stage instead of a date ('Early-stage', 'Multiple rounds', 'Growth'). An ISO date plus a precision field (day, month, quarter, year) and an optional note would make these machine-safe.

examples.note: Stage text in the date field; all other round fields null.

findings.description: In investor-first rows the country is null in 224 of 1200 rows, and 87 values carry a city or a second country ('Sweden (Stockholm)', 'UK (London)' next to 'United Kingdom (London)', 'Estonia (HQ Los Angeles)', 'South Africa / Estonia'). An ISO country code plus an hq_city field would fix this.

We cross-checked 60 random rounds that /v1/knowledge/query returned with a named lead (2019 onward, mostly European) against the FundingRound entities in the graph, following your field guide (company -> outgoing PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND role ISSUER -> FundingRound -> incoming PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND with is_lead). The graph had a matching round (same stage label, within a year) for 7 of 60. For 51 of 60 the company entity had no FundingRound edges at all. Recent Nordic seed rounds behind our demo were mostly absent (25 of 30 not found).
examples: Sono (seed, Jun 2026): company entity has no rounds
Metaktik: graph has only a Pre-Seed round, not the 2026 seed

findings.description: Where the graph has the round and marks is_lead, it agreed with the lead from the query layer in 6 of 6 sample rounds (VOI Series A: Balderton; Anyfin Series C: Northzone; Parafin Series B: GIC; and others). Ranked sources (FILING / PRIMARY / PRESS) made each check easy to verify.

Some FundingRound entities seem to merge several rounds. Lovable's SERIES_B entity (announced 2025-12-18, USD 425m) marks 6 investors as is_lead: Menlo Ventures, CapitalG, Accel, Creandum, byFounders and Hummingbird. Accel led the Series A, Creandum the 2025 seed and byFounders/Hummingbird the 2024 pre-seed. Lovable has only SERIES_B and SERIES_C as round entities. TesterArmy's SEED entity also marks 5 leads of 32 participants.

One fund appears as several entities, and the funding-round edges sit on only one of them. 'Creandum' resolves to 6 entities (Creandum Kommanditbolag, Creandum Fund, Creandum, Creandum Advisor LLP, Creandum Advisor AB, Creandum III L.P.). The entity id that /v1/knowledge/query returns for Creandum (7d4ebd18, 'Creandum Fund') has no PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND edges; Creandum Kommanditbolag has 5. Likewise the Lovable id returned by the query layer (a1a12886) has no round edges, while the Company entity found by name search (d6725096) does. A link from query-layer entity ids to the canonical graph entity would let users go from a query answer straight to the graph.
One is_lead participant on a SEED round (Solarock, 2022) is the entity 'Renewable Energy industry', an industry rather than an investor.

We checked the rounds behind one fund's 'does the lead come back?' record (Lifeline Ventures, 10 cases) and four Creandum seed leads from Oct 2026 against press releases and the fund's own portfolio page. Most rows hold. These five do not: a round label and amount that mix equity and debt, an investor listed in a round no source puts it in, a round no public source mentions, a wrong company country, and a co-lead returned as a participant. Each example gives the raw Cala row and the source URL. Checked 2026-11-14 by web search, no LLM judging.

examples.issue: Round label and amount: the USD 117m round of Apr 2026 was equity led by Lifeline Ventures plus debt from Nordic lenders, with no series label in the announcement. Cala returns it as 'Series A (follow-on)' in one investor-first row and as 'Other Equity' dated 'Dec 2025' in another, both with the full USD 117m. Lifeline's own portfolio page labels its 2026 Verda investment 'Series B'.

Participant not supported: Cala lists Lifeline Ventures among the investors of the Nov 2016 EUR 5m Series A. TechCrunch and tech.eu name only Joi Ito and Jaan Tallinn; Lifeline's own portfolio page says the 2016 Series A was led by David Shuman and Harpreet Rai and lists Lifeline again only from the 2021 Series C. Cala also returns no lead for this round while Lifeline's page names two.

raw_row.other_investors: Lifeline Ventures, Joi Ito, Nat Turner, Jaan Tallinn (Future of Life Institute)

examples.issue: Round with no public source: Cala returns a seed round dated 'January 1, 2024 (approximate)', amount and investors 'Not publicly disclosed'; Cala's own knowledge answer attributes it to PitchBook. We found no press for it, and Lifeline's portfolio page lists only a 2023 pre-seed and the Oct 2026 seed (led by b2venture, with Lifeline). For a 'did the lead come back?' count, this placeholder round becomes the 'next round' and the fund is counted as not returning.
Country: Cala returns 'UK'. The company is based in Basel, Switzerland (tech.eu: 'Swiss startup Atlas Bio'). The lead (Creandum) and the USD 10m seed amount are correct.

Co-lead returned as participant: the investor-first row has lead 'Creandum' and participant 'Lakestar'. Press reports the round as co-led by Creandum and Lakestar, and Cala's own /v1/knowledge/search answer for the same round also names both as leads.

note_on_counts: The example counts in each finding were measured on the snapshot available when the finding was written (about 43 funds asked investor-first). The patterns hold on the larger final snapshot; the live app shows current totals.
